key_insight: Successful negotiation requires executable value, not just agreement: TACTIC improves economic outcomes by adapting to prior settlement results without updating base LLM weights.
engineering_relevance: Multi-agent systems should validate negotiated commitments against operational constraints and use execution feedback to refine future strategies.
method: TradeWar converts multi-country negotiations into tariff and trade-share policies, enforcing capacity and network constraints at settlement.
Outcomes are scored using an Economic Health Index (EHI).
TACTIC refines strategies across episodes using prior experience, opponent behavior, and settlement outcomes.
evidence_signal: Across 20 sequential episodes and three seeds, TACTIC’s final EHI (×100) rose from 58.2 to 73.2, versus 65.2 for an ablation without cross-episode updates.
watch_item: Evaluation is simulation-based and uses three seeds; transfer to real trade negotiations remains unestablished.
paper_title: TradeWar: A Benchmark for Execution-Grounded Trade Negotiation with Adaptive LLM Agents
